recorded: 2026-09-28, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook), Gemma 4 26B-A4B UD-Q4_K_XL, 512 prompt / 128 output
candidate: merge the Q5_1 expert down MMQ's inner-loop memory traffic. The kernel issued 24 scalar memory operations per (row, sub-block) against 16 sudot4: load_qs_bytes fetched each weight qword as four byte loads or-ed together, the weight nibble planes and high-bit expansions were rebuilt for every row of a dynamically-bounded row loop, and the eight activation dwords of a sub-block were eight separate dword loads.
reason: a load-width and loop-invariant change, not an arithmetic one. The byte-or-chain and the single dword load produce the same value, the hoisted expressions depend only on the sub-block, and the two uint4 loads read the same eight dwords the scalar loads read. No floating-point operation moved or changed, so the output is bit-identical, and that is measured below rather than argued.

geometry.route_share: 124.2 ms of an 829.5 ms prefill (15.0%) after the change, against 162.4 ms (18.9%) before, from scripts/gemma4_prefill_kernel_census.py

performance.protocol: one declared same-host protocol measuring both arms in the same session: scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py --prompt 512 --output 128 --samples 3 --warmup 1, with the parent revision of the one changed file restored into the worktree for the baseline arm and the committed revision for the candidate arm. Nothing else differs between the arms.

decode.why: not incidental. gemma4_moe_prefill_route_enabled keys on the runner's declared width rather than the live row count, by design, so a runner built for 512 tokens takes this same MMQ kernel on its single-token decode steps. The route is therefore a property of the runner and the fix reaches both phases.

kernel_isolation.at_1024_tokens: 5.347 to 4.031 ms per layer, the same -24.6%, so the fix is not specific to the 512-token operating point

performance.control: the Q4_K gate_up kernel, launched 29 times per prefill against the same rows, is unchanged within noise (5.246 to 5.309 ms per layer). It stages its weight and activation tiles through LDS caches rather than re-reading global memory, which is why it was already at 54.4 GB/s and why the down projection was the outlier.
